thesis: Method-test thesis: about three quarters of Sunflag's value is a 10.66% stake in Lloyds Metals & Energy (post-tax ~Rs 9,016 cr vs a Rs 6,643 cr market cap); the special-steel business compounds ~8%/yr at ~7% NOPAT margin with ROIIC close to the cost of equity, and the market's ~50% discount on the stake persists over 5 years unless the stake is monetised and distributed.
variant_view: Market (reverse DCF): at Rs 368.60 the price implies either a 45-61% discount on the post-tax LMEL stake (if the steel business is worth our bear-to-bull DCF of Rs 93-170/share) or, at a 55% discount, 5.4x EV/EBITDA and 12.5x P/E for steel (KSL 12.6x). Our view: the gap is NOT a mispricing we can claim. The discount sits inside the Indian holdco base range (insight:group-holdco-discount) and is justified by three things we verified: no stated monetisation or payout policy (dividend Re 1, ~9% payout), the stake already serves as loan collateral (74 lakh LMEL shares pledged to Indian Bank), and management is spending on a 10-block mining programme with a weak delivery record (Lohardongri LOI 2019, still not operating; Belgaon reserve figure stale for a year). What we add that the market may underweight: the steel balance sheet is now near debt-free (net debt Rs 26 cr at Sep-2026, CRISIL AA-/Stable) and the business earns a ~14% pre-tax ROCE, so the bear case is LMEL-driven, not steel-driven. What would prove us wrong: (a) a board decision to sell LMEL shares with a buyback/special dividend (gap closes; our 'persists' call fails), or (b) LMEL proceeds or new debt going into mining capex (discount widens; our steel-is-safe view fails). Departure from the outside view (card §5): our P(>=3x in 5y) is far below the base class and P(<=0.5x) above it on purpose. The class is survivors of the 2020-25 small-cap bull run (x3 overstated, losses understated, per its caveats); Sunflag's 5-year outcome is ~75% a single listed stock (LMEL, already up ~3.2x in 3 years) held at a discount, plus a steel business whose ROIIC is close to the cost of equity, so a 3x needs LMEL to roughly triple again or the discount to close; the fatter left tail is single-stock concentration (beta 0.73 to LMEL). These 5-year card calls are the cleanest test in this file of whether our structural adjustment beats the naive class. Checked by paper calls thesis:paper-call:SUNFLAG:* (6 operating/event/price calls to 2027-09-30, plus the 3 card calls).

pre_mortem: LMEL fell 50% on an iron-ore royalty or Gadchiroli mining shock; Sunflag fell ~35% with it although steel did fine (beta to LMEL 0.73, weekly corr 0.54 over 2 years).
The board sold part of the LMEL stake to fund Tambia South / Bhivkund mining capex instead of returning cash; the market widened the discount to 70%.
A steel-import surge (China/Korea/Japan, flagged in AR26) compressed the SBQ spread; OPM fell to 8-9% and the steel stub de-rated to 4x EBITDA.
A promoter-family or trust (Zedra, Jersey) restructuring or a Daido exit created supply overhang in an illiquid stock (ADV Rs 13.5 cr).
